speaker: Miriam Levy
text: My parents came to London in 1956 with one suitcase between them.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: They had lost almost everyone in the war, and they didn't talk about it for many years.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: What they did talk about was the future. Education, education, education.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: I was the first in our family to go to university, and my mother cried at the graduation.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: Faith was quiet in our house. Shabbat candles, the prayers my father hummed while shaving.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: When my husband was ill, it was the synagogue community that carried us.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: Meals on the doorstep every night for three months. People I barely knew.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: I learned then that a community is not a building, it's people who notice.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: Um, I suppose, um, I worry sometimes that young people feel alone, you know, on their phones.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: But then I see my granddaughter running the charity bake sale and I have hope.

speaker: Miriam Levy
text: If I could pass on one thing, it would be gratitude. Say thank you, every day.
